svg.title: How com-morpheus-plugin works
svg.desc: Architecture and request flows of com-morpheus-plugin: the browser, the plugin inside the Morpheus appliance, and the HPE Compute Ops Management API in GreenLake.
svg.text: Shows HPE Compute Ops Management (COM) data for physical HPE servers inside Morpheus, and runs a few safe COM jobs.
Morpheus web UI: nothing to install
Links: Open in COM, Open iLO
One row per host: COM match,
Each click is a POST that carries
and the tab's signed action token. Job
Decide where a tab appears: HPE
Render the tab's HTML on the
The script acts only inside the
COM tab, with a fixed list of
the security gates in D below
Builds tab and cluster data, with
HTTPS to the COM API, optional
Issues a token for the API client
One shared identity for the whole
Six fixed job templates: UID on,
Morpheus data the plugin reads (it never writes)
Hosts and their hardware vendor · network-interface MAC addresses · tags
com-serial / com-id · cluster membership · the user's tenant, roles and
permissions · plugin settings (the API client secret stays here and never
The browser never calls GreenLake. Open iLO
is a plain link to the iLO's address.
only. Nothing in GreenLake calls Morpheus.
A. Matching a host to a COM server
The plugin compares globally unique MACs
Result: Confirmed (all MACs on one COM
server), Probable, Conflict or No match.
A com-serial= or com-id= tag can choose
the server shown. For actions, the tag
must agree with the host's own MACs.
No agent, no SSH, no iLO login: only data
Morpheus asks the tab provider whether to
show the tab: HPE hardware, physical
ComService looks up the host's match. On
first use the index builds in the
background and the tab says so.
ComClient reads the server, alerts, iLO
Reads are cached: server and alerts 1
min, security 5 min, groups 1 h, warranty
The appliance renders the HTML and adds a
signed action token for that host.
Server list and warranties: one read each
for the whole cluster. Active alerts: one
workspace query where COM allows it,
One row per host: match, model, serial,
maintenance, links to the host and to
Totals: hosts in COM, health, hosts with
Read-only. No buttons on this tab.
Every gate must pass, in this order:
Role has Run HPE COM actions (full)
Signed action token for this host
Host is in the user's tenant and is a
Confirmed MAC match (a tag must agree)
No action on this server in the last 30 s
ComService creates the COM job and logs
The browser polls the job's progress
Every read and every job uses one GreenLake API client that the administrator configures in the plugin settings. COM sees that client, not the Morpheus user. Morpheus roles
decide who can see the tabs (View HPE COM data) and who can press the buttons (Run HPE COM actions). Each job is logged in Morpheus with the user who started it.
